questions_and_answers.question_text: What was the original meaning of gài?
When were the Ten Great Structures built, and by whom?

answers.answer_text: In the 1950s, designed and built by the Chinese themselves.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Why were the Ten Great Structures built?

answers.answer_text: To modernize the layout of the capital and at the same time commemorate the revolutionary victory and its heroes.
To appreciate, to enjoy, to admire.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Name five of the Ten Great Structures.
Translate into Chinese: How many years has it been since this house was built?
What architectural styles are found among the Ten Great Structures?
Translate into Chinese: I really admire the Ten Great Structures you've built since liberation.
Which verb, gài or jiànzhù, would you use for a road, and why?

articles.text:
9. A: Wǒ hěn xīnshǎng nǐmen jiěfàng yǐhòu gàide Shí Dà Jiànzhù.
   I really admire the Ten Great Structures you've built since liberation.
   B: Nín tài kèqi le.
   You're too polite.

Notes on No. 9

gài: "to build," only used for buildings. (Another common use of this word is as the verb "to cover," which was the original meaning.)

Zhèige fángzi gàile duōshǎo nián le?
How old is this house/building? (lit., "How many years has it been since this house was built?")

Shí Dà Jiànzhù: The "Ten Great Structures" in Běijīng were designed and built in the 1950s by the Chinese themselves. The authorities wanted to modernize the layout of the capital and at the same time to commemorate the revolutionary victory and its heroes. The architectural styles include Western as well as traditional Chinese. The buildings are as follows: Běijīng Railroad Station, Museum of Art, Museum of History, Great Hall of the People, Revolutionary Military Museum, Telegraph Building, Nationalities Cultural Palace, Agricultural Exhibition Hall, Workers Stadium, and the Monument to the People's Heroes.
